claim: The final v2.1 metrics are approved. This session does not change those figures; it evaluates where the system fails under more realistic conditions.
Recall@10 falls from 81.7 to 75.2 percent for abbreviated queries and to 72.9 percent for typographical errors. Temporal questions retain 78.4 percent, but fail when dates are expressed relatively.
English has more errors involving administrative names translated non-literally. In Spanish, the main problem is ambiguous acronyms.
Approved. v2.1 remains frozen; acronym expansion, typographical normalization and relative-date handling will be evaluated as candidates for v2.2.
